states.name: q
states.meaning: 16-bit 4-digit BCD counter value: q[3:0]=ones, q[7:4]=tens, q[11:8]=hundreds, q[15:12]=thousands.
states.update_time: posedge clk after settled; synchronous active-high reset overrides increment.

rules.condition: reset==1 at a posedge clk; q is cleared to 0 after the edge. Reset has priority over the BCD increment.
reset==0 at a posedge clk; q increments by one as a 4-digit BCD number modulo 10000, with q[3:0]=ones, q[7:4]=tens, q[11:8]=hundreds, q[15:12]=thousands.

Combinational from current q. Let ones=q[3:0], tens=q[7:4], hundreds=q[11:8]. Numeric ena uses bit0 for digit1/tens enable, bit1 for digit2/hundreds enable, bit2 for digit3/thousands enable: bit0=(ones==9); bit1=(ones==9 && tens==9); bit2=(ones==9 && tens==9 && hundreds==9); ena = bit0 + 2*bit1 + 4*bit2.
rules.spec_quote: For digits [3:1], also output an enable signal indicating when each of the upper three digits should be incremented.

reset.name: reset
reset.first_released_cycle: the first posedge clk at which reset is low; q may increment from 0 on that edge

before.mid: No mid-cycle input changes are required by the examples; reset is applied before the sampled posedge of each row.

uncertain.note: The spec names a synchronous active-high reset but does not explicitly state the reset value or precedence over counting.
candidates: reset clears q to 0 and overrides increment
reset value is unspecified or non-zero

uncertain.note: The exact packing/timing of the 3-bit ena output is inferred from BCD carry behavior and digit numbering.
candidates: ena bit0=tens enable, bit1=hundreds enable, bit2=thousands enable, combinational from q
ena bits use reversed digit ordering or are registered on posedge

uncertain.note: The spec only names a 4-digit BCD counter; the up-count direction, +1 increment, modulo 10000 wrap, and posedge update are inferred conventions.
candidates: increments by one as a 4-digit BCD number modulo 10000 on posedge clk
down-counts or has unspecified increment direction/modulus/timing
